# 工具目录（Tool Catalog）

本目录穷举 pi-web 的内置工具面。每个变体的工具集合都不是手抄源码，而是来自真实 runtime 的模型请求：生成脚本以 demo 模式启动 runtime（与 `tests/prompt-snapshot.test.ts` 同一条生产线），向每个变体发送一条探测消息，捕获到达 provider 的请求并读取其中的工具清单。MCP 动态工具与插件提供的工具不在本目录内。

变体含义：`default` 为默认会话（code mode on，全量工具）；`plan` 为计划模式会话；`readonly` 为只读会话；`subagent-general` / `subagent-explore` 为 `subagent` 委派出的子智能体（general / explore profile）。总表按 default 变体的注册序排列，✓ 表示该变体的请求里出现了这个工具，— 表示被该变体的工具过滤排除。

## tool read

Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "path"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)"
    },
    "offset": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)"
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Maximum number of lines to read"
    }
  }
}
```

## tool edit

Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "path",
    "edits"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)"
    },
    "edits": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": [
          "oldText",
          "newText"
        ],
        "properties": {
          "oldText": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call."
          },
          "newText": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "Replacement text for this targeted edit."
          }
        }
      },
      "description": "One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead."
    }
  }
}
```

## tool bash

Execute a bash command and return its stdout/stderr. Prefer the dedicated tools over shell equivalents: content search → the grep tool; file discovery → glob; a known file path → read; in-place edits → edit. Do not use `grep -r`, `rg`, `find`, or recursive `ls` for workspace-wide search. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked, and guard path variables so an unset value cannot widen the target. Do not run dev servers, watch modes or interactive programs in the foreground; they hold the call until the timeout. Prefer one-shot forms and non-interactive flags (for example `vitest run`, `tsc --noEmit`, `git commit -m`). Commands still running after 15s are moved to the background and their output is saved to a file; use read on that path to check progress. Long output is truncated to its tail and the full output is saved to a temp file. Check the exit code before moving on.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "command"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "command": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Bash command to execute"
    },
    "description": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words."
    },
    "workdir": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it."
    },
    "timeout": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Timeout in seconds (default 300). Pass a larger value for long builds or test suites."
    }
  }
}
```

## tool list_files

List relative file and directory paths from the current workspace. path defaults to "."; recursive defaults to false; maxEntries is an integer from 1 to 100 (default 100). Hidden paths, node_modules, common secret files, and symlinks are excluded. Read-only; does not invoke a shell.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 1024
    },
    "recursive": {
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "maxEntries": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "maximum": 100
    }
  }
}
```

Returns relative paths, one-based line numbers, and excerpts. path defaults to "."; recursive defaults to true; maxResults is an integer from 1 to 50 (default 50). ## tool glob

Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. A pattern without "/" matches the basename at any depth; "**" matches any depth. Includes hidden paths; excludes VCS metadata, node_modules, dist, .data, common secret files, and symlinks. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order (newest first). Read-only; no shell. Prefer this over find or ls -R.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "pattern"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "pattern": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "maxLength": 1024
    },
    "path": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 1024
    },
    "maxResults": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "maximum": 100
    }
  }
}
```

Source: [src/server/tools/research.ts](../src/server/tools/research.ts)

## tool grep

Search workspace text files with a regular expression (native ripgrep, with a JavaScript fallback; case-insensitive by default). Use this to find unknown content or file locations; use read directly when you know the file path. Do not run `grep` or `rg` via shell: they bypass workspace policy, output limits, and sensitive-file filtering. Patterns use ripgrep regex syntax when the native engine runs; if ripgrep rejects a pattern, the JavaScript fallback is tried. path defaults to "."; include optionally filters files by glob (for example "*.ts"); maxResults is an integer from 1 to 50 (default 50). Skips hidden paths, node_modules, common secret files, binary/oversized files and symlinks. Read-only; no shell.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "pattern"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "pattern": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "maxLength": 1024
    },
    "path": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 1024
    },
    "include": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 1024
    },
    "caseSensitive": {
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "maxResults": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "maximum": 50
    }
  }
}
```

## tool browser

Drive a headless Chromium browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol — for UI verification and page checks that shell tools cannot do (rendering bugs, web consoles, visual smoke checks). Actions: "open" navigates (url required) and returns title/URL/page text; "evaluate" runs a JS expression in the page (expression required); "click" clicks the first CSS-selector match (selector required); "fill" sets an input/textarea value and fires input/change events (selector + value required); "screenshot" returns a PNG as an image block (fullPage optional); "close" shuts the browser down. The browser launches once per pi-web process with an isolated profile and tabs are reused across calls; pass freshProfile to wipe the profile on launch. Screenshots are expensive — prefer evaluate/text assertions when they suffice.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "action"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "open"
        },
        {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "evaluate"
        },
        {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "click"
        },
        {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "fill"
        },
        {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "screenshot"
        },
        {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "close"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Operation to perform."
    },
    "url": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Absolute URL for the open action (http, https or file)."
    },
    "expression": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "JavaScript expression for the evaluate action."
    },
    "selector": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "CSS selector for the click/fill actions."
    },
    "value": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Value for the fill action."
    },
    "fullPage": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Capture beyond the viewport for the screenshot action."
    },
    "freshProfile": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Wipe the browser profile before launching (open action)."
    }
  }
}
```

## tool todo_write

Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip trivial single-step work. Add one concrete step per item before starting, including relevant verification. Replace the entire list on every call, so include every current item; anything omitted is removed. Update statuses promptly as work changes and mark an item completed as soon as it is done. Mark an item in_progress only while actively working on it; use multiple in_progress items only for work actually running in parallel. Do not use the list as a substitute for the plan-mode plan; it tracks steps you are actually carrying out.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "todos"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "todos": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": [
          "content",
          "status"
        ],
        "properties": {
          "content": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "status": {
            "anyOf": [
              {
                "type": "string",
                "const": "pending"
              },
              {
                "type": "string",
                "const": "in_progress"
              },
              {
                "type": "string",
                "const": "completed"
              }
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## tool schedule_create

Create a scheduled task. At each occurrence of rrule, prompt is delivered to the target session as a scheduled message from the user. The result includes the task id and the next occurrence. After downtime, only the latest missed occurrence is delivered.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "title",
    "prompt",
    "rrule",
    "target"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "title": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Task name of at most 120 characters in the user's language: action plus object. Omit timing, status, ids, and bracketed suffixes."
    },
    "prompt": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Instruction delivered at each occurrence."
    },
    "rrule": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "RFC 5545 subset: one DTSTART line, a newline, and one RRULE line. DTSTART ends in Z for UTC or carries TZID with an IANA time zone; a fixed offset such as UTC+5 is Etc/GMT-5, with the sign reversed. A TZID rule keeps local clock time across daylight-saving changes; generated nonexistent local times are skipped, and repeated ones occur once, at the earlier instant. DTSTART may be in the past; delivery starts with the first occurrence after creation. A one-time delivery is RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=1. Supported: FREQ=MINUTELY, HOURLY, DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, YEARLY; COUNT at most 1000; UNTIL as a UTC instant ending in Z. MINUTELY and HOURLY accept no BY parts, so set the clock time in DTSTART. BYMONTHDAY and ordinal BYDAY require MONTHLY or YEARLY; BYYEARDAY and BYWEEKNO require YEARLY; an ordinal BYDAY cannot combine with BYWEEKNO. Example: \"DTSTART;TZID=Asia/Shanghai:20260901T080000\\nRRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR;BYSETPOS=-1\""
    },
    "target": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "this_session"
        },
        {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "new_once"
        },
        {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "new"
        }
      ],
      "description": "this_session delivers to this session; new_once delivers to the same new session every time, opened at the first delivery; new opens a different new session for every delivery. New sessions use this session's working directory. Use this_session for reminders and for follow-ups to this conversation; use new_once or new for independent work, such as a recurring report, and whenever the user asks for a new conversation."
    }
  }
}
```

Source: [src/server/tools/schedule.ts](../src/server/tools/schedule.ts)

## tool wetrack_analysis_save

Persist the analysis of one WeTrack defect so the issues page can show it after the conversation is gone. Pass the answer body you would send to the user as `markdown`; the page renders it verbatim. Read wetrack_analysis_get first and provide the returned revision as expectedRevision. A stale revision is rejected. A blocked attempt preserves any previous analyzed or fixed conclusion. Call again with status "fixed" only after the user approves and the fix is done.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "defectNumber",
    "markdown",
    "expectedRevision"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "defectNumber": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 4,
      "maxLength": 32,
      "description": "DTS 编号，例如 DTS006761203"
    },
    "markdown": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
```

## tool ask_user_question

Ask the user up to eight questions (usually one to three) and end this turn without waiting for the answer. Use this when a user-owned choice, missing external reference, or material ambiguity blocks progress; do not use it for facts you can inspect in the workspace. Ask brief, direct, self-contained questions in user-facing terms; assume the user does not know background work or internal names. Each question has a stable id, the question text, optional options (label plus optional description), and multiSelect. If you recommend one option, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to its label. The answers arrive as a follow-up user message on a later turn; continue with independent work or wrap up now. Pending is not permission: do not perform the action a pending question depends on; a timeout or unanswered question is not consent. Do not repeat the same questions while they are pending.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "questions"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "questions": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": [
          "id",
          "question"
        ],
        "properties": {
          "id": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "header": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "question": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "options": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "object",
              "required": [
                "label"
              ],
              "properties": {
                "label": {
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "description": {
                  "type": "string"
                }
              }
            }
          },
          "multiSelect": {
            "type": "boolean"
          }
        }
      },
      "minItems": 1,
      "maxItems": 8
    }
  }
}
```

## tool enter_plan_mode

Switch this conversation into plan mode yourself, without asking the user and without waiting for a confirmation. Prefer entering plan mode for implementation tasks unless they are trivial: new features, work with several viable approaches, multi-file refactors, architectural decisions, or unclear acceptance criteria. Simple lookups, one-line fixes, obvious bug fixes, direct answers, and tasks with explicit and detailed user instructions do not need plan mode. While plan mode is active, only research the repository and design the plan — make no changes — and finish by submitting the plan with exit_plan_mode for the user's approval. If plan mode is already active, there is no need to call this again.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {}
}
```

Source: [src/server/tools/plan.ts](../src/server/tools/plan.ts)

## tool exit_plan_mode

Submit the plan you wrote in plan mode for the user's approval, ending this turn without waiting for the review. Use it only when the task is code-writing work whose implementation steps need planning; for research tasks — gathering information, searching or reading files, understanding the codebase — answer directly instead and do not submit a plan. Before calling, make sure the plan is complete and unambiguous: resolve any material user-owned questions about requirements or approach first, then submit. Do not separately ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" — submitting the plan is itself the approval request. Make this the only and final tool call in that assistant response, and make the plan Markdown starting with a level-1 heading ("# <title>") followed by the steps and the verification you will run. Only call this while plan mode is active. The user reviews the plan in the transcript; approval turns plan mode off and their confirmation arrives as a follow-up message. If they ask for changes, revise the plan and call exit_plan_mode again instead of starting the work. Examples: "search for and understand how vim mode is implemented" → report the findings, do not submit a plan; "implement yank mode for vim" → submit the implementation plan; "add authentication, auth method undecided" → ask which auth method first, then submit.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "plan"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "plan": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

## tool subagent

Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent: a separate agent that works in its own conversation and returns its result, not its intermediate steps. It inherits this conversation's agent configuration — tools, model, working directory — but not its messages, so make the task self-contained: state the task, scope, applicable constraints and authorization, acceptance criteria, whether the task is read-only or permits writing, and the result evidence to return. Specify a return format when it matters. The child shares the working directory; assign disjoint write paths and require it to preserve changes outside its assigned scope. agent_type picks a built-in profile — general-purpose (default, inherits this conversation's working tools, without planning, user questions, goal or delegation tools) or Explore (read-only search: broad codebase sweeps where you only need the conclusion; state the search breadth "medium" or "very thorough" in the task). model optionally selects the child's model as {provider, modelId}, validated against the catalog and allowlist; omit to inherit this conversation's model. Use when: answering means reading across many files (you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps), or independent work worth running separately. Do NOT delegate single-fact lookups where you already know the file/symbol — search directly. Once you delegate a search, do not also run it yourself; wait for the result. This call waits for the subagent to finish and returns its final answer as the tool result; relay what matters to the user. Set run_in_background to true to launch without waiting: the call returns immediately, you keep working, and the subagent's result arrives later as a follow-up message (a settlement notice); do not wait for it or end your turn just to wait.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "task"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "task": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "label": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "agent_type": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "general-purpose"
        },
        {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "Explore"
        }
      ]
    },
    "model": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": [
        "provider",
        "modelId"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "provider": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "modelId": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      }
    },
    "run_in_background": {
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  }
}
```

## tool spawn_teammate

Create one named, durable teammate in a separate child conversation; it runs in the background and this call returns without waiting for its answer. Only the Team Lead may call this tool. The name must be unique lower-kebab-case, at most 64 characters, and never "lead"; a name is never reused, even after a failed creation. The prompt is the teammate's complete, self-contained initial task: it inherits your agent configuration, tools, model and working directory, but not your messages. Include the task, assigned scope, applicable constraints and authorization, acceptance criteria, and required result evidence. context picks the seed: fresh starts an empty child, fork continues from your last completed turn. model optionally selects a fresh teammate's model as {provider, modelId}, validated against the catalog and allowlist; a fork keeps your model to preserve the prefix it reuses, so model is rejected with context: "fork". Members share the working directory. Assign disjoint write scopes and require the teammate to preserve edits outside its assigned scope. Teammates are for genuine collaboration that needs the shared task board or member-to-member messaging over time. Independent one-shot subtasks — even many in parallel, even cross-checking each other — belong to subagent instead: its tool result returns the subagent's answer directly, while a teammate's final text never flows back to the Lead on its own (collect it through tasks, messages, or files).

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "name",
    "prompt"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "description": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "prompt": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "context": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "fresh"
        },
        {
          "type": "string",
          "const": "fork"
        }
      ]
    },
    "model": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": [
        "provider",
        "modelId"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "provider": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "modelId": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## tool codemode

Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers. - `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. A tool whose declaration returns an object resolves on failure too when it returned that object; check its fields. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled. - The script survives a restart: it resumes where it was, without running finished calls again. - Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`  Globals: - `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path. - `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls. - `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find tools the `codemode` section does not list.  `models` (all functions return promises): - `models.getModelsOfType(type, provider?)`, `models.getAvailableOfType(type, provider?)` (configured auth only), `models.getModelOfType(type, provider, id)`: the catalog; `type` is "chat", "image", or "classifier". - `models.classify(model, { state: { ... }, images?: [{ type: "image", data, mimeType }], questions: { <id>: { type: "choice", instructions, criteria: { <label>: <meaning> } } | { type: "score", instructions, criteria: [<lowest level>, ..., <highest level>] } | { type: "bool", instructions, criteria: { true: <meaning>, false: <meaning> } } } })` resolves to `{ answers: { <id>: ... }, stopReason, errorMessage?, usage? }`. - `models.generateImages(model, { input: [{ type: "text", text: <prompt> }, ...optional { type: "image", data, mimeType }] })` resolves to `{ output: [image blocks], stopReason, errorMessage?, usage? }`; show each image with `image(block)`. At most 4 classify/generateImages calls run at once; more wait.  The `codemode` section of the system prompt lists the tools scripts can call, by namespace, as far as space allows.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "code"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "code": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Raw JavaScript source."
    }
  }
}
```

Source: [src/server/codemode-policy.ts](../src/server/codemode-policy.ts)
